# Theme tokens

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-token-docs.mjs. Do not edit by hand:
     test/build/token_docs_drift.test.ts fails if this file and the
     token sources disagree. Re-run the script instead. -->

Every value the theme renders comes from one of these CSS custom properties. They are the public styling API: set any of them from the stylesheet you point [`css`](config-schema.md) at, and the whole site follows.

## Overriding

Your stylesheet loads after the theme's, and the theme's own CSS is wrapped in a `@layer ocx` cascade layer. Any rule you write is unlayered, and an unlayered rule beats a layered one **at any specificity** — so you never need `!important` and never need to out-specify an internal selector.

```css
:root {
  --ocx-color-accent: #2563eb;
  --ocx-radius-lg: 0; /* square corners everywhere */
}

.dark {
  --ocx-color-accent: #60a5fa;
}
```

**Set both blocks.** `:root` and `.dark` have the same specificity and both match `<html>`, so a `:root`-only override wins in dark mode too and pins that token to its light value. Overriding only `:root` is the single most common way to accidentally break dark mode.

A token whose default is shown as `var(--ocx-…)` is an **alias**: it follows whatever that token resolves to, in both colour schemes, so it needs no `.dark` entry of its own.
